solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Peacekeeper unhappy about splitting risk (4,5)

indicatorNotes.splitting: RE splits BET in two, sitting between its B and its ET

blocks.note: blue = sad, down
a bet is a risk you take on an outcome
re = about, as in a memo heading

annotation.surface: A peacekeeping soldier, glum about a dangerous posting.
annotation.walkthrough: The UN's peacekeeping troops wear blue berets, so the nickname names the soldier by the hat.
annotation.definitionFit: A blue beret is a United Nations peacekeeper, named after the headgear.

entries.clue: One inclined to show respect and retreat (5)

blocks.note: someone who bows, bending forward in respect
a noun here: a shady, leafy nook in a garden, a place to retreat to

annotation.surface: A deferential courtier bows and backs away from the throne.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Inclined' is literal here: the bower bends at the waist. 'Retreat' looks like the courtier's next move but is a noun, a leafy hideaway.
annotation.definitionFit: One who bows to show respect is a bower; a bower is also a sheltered garden retreat.

entries.clue: Spy less than secret about top grade info (10,5)

indicatorNotes.about: COVERT goes about, around, A and GEN

blocks.note: under = less than, as in under ten
covert = secret
A is the top grade in an exam
gen is British slang for information

annotation.surface: An agent who handles material just below top-secret clearance.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Less than secret' reads as a security classification just below top secret; the solver has to break it into two separate synonyms. Gen is British slang for information.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: an agent working under cover is exactly what the noun spy names.

entries.clue: Full cargo left to feed cold-blooded creatures (8)

indicatorNotes.to feed: L is fed into TOAD, going inside it

blocks.note: a boa is a snake, cold-blooded like the toad
a toad is an amphibian, the second creature
L = left

annotation.surface: Someone tipping a whole shipment of food in for the reptiles at the zoo.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Creatures' is plural because it supplies two animals, BOA and TOAD, and L goes into the second of them.
annotation.definitionFit: A boatload is as much as a boat can carry, a full cargo.

entries.clue: Temper resistance with maturity (4)

blocks.note: R is the symbol for electrical resistance
age = maturity, years

annotation.surface: Advice to calm one's anger as one grows older.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Temper' looks like a verb, to moderate, but it is the noun: a fit of anger.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym for the noun, where temper means an outburst of anger, as in 'flew into a temper'.

entries.clue: Dramatic article by a pilot bagging top speed (10)

indicatorNotes.bagging: TRIAL bags C, holding it inside

blocks.note: the definite article
used as it stands
a pilot scheme is a trial run
c is the speed of light, the fastest possible

annotation.surface: A showy magazine piece about an airman grabbing a speed record.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Pilot' reads as a flyer and 'top speed' as his record; in fact a pilot is a trial, and c, the speed of light, is the top speed of physics.
annotation.definitionFit: Theatrical means dramatic, as of the stage or a showy manner.

entries.clue: Reason to oust a duke or two (5)

indicatorNotes.to oust: one D is ousted, thrown out of DEDUCE

blocks.note: to reason something out is to deduce it
D = duke; the middle D goes

annotation.surface: Grounds for deposing a nobleman or two.
annotation.walkthrough: 'A duke or two' reads as a head count of nobles; 'or' is only a link, and 'two' is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: The deuce is the two in a pack of cards or on a die, a games word for the number.

entries.clue: Society gals bored by we nerdy types (6)

indicatorNotes.bored by: WE bores into DEBS, going inside

blocks.note: debs are debutantes, young women entering high society
used as it stands

annotation.surface: Posh young women yawning at a bunch of geeks who admit to being nerds.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface's ungrammatical 'we nerdy types' is the giveaway that WE is being used as letters.
annotation.definitionFit: Dweebs are socially awkward, studious people: nerdy types.

entries.clue: Dirty plum skins are not unsafe (15)

indicatorNotes.unsafe: the letters are not safely in place, so they get rearranged

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 15 letters

annotation.surface: A food-safety note: grubby plum skins are fine to eat.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Dirty' sits beside plum skins as if describing fruit, but it is dirty as in foul play.
annotation.definitionFit: Dirty play is unsportsmanlike, against the spirit of fair competition.

entries.clue: German city chess champ holds one prerequisite (9)

indicatorNotes.holds: to hold something is to have it in your grasp, so TAL wraps round I

blocks.note: Essen is a city in the Ruhr
Mikhail Tal, world chess champion 1960
I = one, the Roman numeral

annotation.surface: A chess champion from a German city holds a first requirement for success.
annotation.walkthrough: Mikhail Tal is the crossword's usual chess champion, because his short name makes useful letters.
annotation.definitionFit: Something essential is a prerequisite, a thing that must come first.

entries.clue: Camera parts we see selling and going wrong (4-5,6)

indicatorNotes.going wrong: the letters go wrong, into a new order

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 15 letters

annotation.surface: A camera shop owner watching their stock sell and malfunction.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a shopkeeper's lament, and 'Camera parts' sits comfortably with it as though it were merely the stock in question.
annotation.definitionFit: Wide-angle lenses are camera lenses with a short focal length, taking in a broad view.

entries.clue: Very little bank to confine a river (6)

indicatorNotes.to confine: RELY confines A and R inside it

blocks.note: to bank on someone is to rely on them
used as it stands
R = river, as on maps

annotation.surface: A modest embankment built to hold a river in.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bank' paints a riverbank but works as a verb: to bank on is to rely.
annotation.definitionFit: Doing something very little is doing it rarely, as in 'she travels very little'.

entries.clue: Firm delivered after objections withdrawn (8)

indicatorNotes.withdrawn: BUTS is drawn back, so it reads backwards
indicatorNotes.after: after means following in order, so BORN follows STUB

blocks.note: ifs and buts: objections
a delivered baby is born

annotation.surface: A company handing something over once complaints were dropped.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Firm' reads as a company, but the definition is the adjective: unyielding.
annotation.definitionFit: Firm here is the adjective, as in 'she stood firm', a plain synonym for unwilling to budge.

entries.clue: One stops flow of travel round Tokyo market we hear (10)

indicatorNotes.we hear: the pieces are spoken, and the answer is spelt as they sound

blocks.note: a tour is travel round a place; it sounds as it is spelt
the Nikkei is the Tokyo stock market index

annotation.surface: A traffic jam holds up a tour of Tokyo's markets.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Flow' suggests traffic but means blood: a tourniquet is tied round a limb to stop bleeding. Said the British way, tourniquet ends like Nikkei.
annotation.definitionFit: A tourniquet is a band tightened round a limb to stop the flow of blood.

entries.clue: What’s in store for me are irresistible temptations (10)

annotation.definition: What’s in store for me are irresistible temptations

blocks.note: the surface pushes fate, what the future holds for the speaker; the setter means the goods on a shop's shelves
to a compulsive buyer, every item on those shelves is a temptation they cannot refuse

annotation.surface: Someone foreseeing a future full of temptations.
annotation.walkthrough: 'What's in store for me' sounds like fate, what the future holds; read literally it is the goods in a store, and the person who cannot resist them is a shopaholic.
annotation.definitionFit: A shopaholic is a compulsive shopper, for whom everything on the shelves is a temptation.

entries.clue: Rooms reported by spy as best place to make contact (5,4)

blocks.note: suites are sets of rooms
to spy something is to spot it

annotation.surface: A secret agent's report on hotel rooms as a good place to meet a contact.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Spy' reads as a noun, the agent, but works as a verb: to spot. 'Make contact' is a bat meeting a ball, not an agent meeting a source.
annotation.definitionFit: The sweet spot on a bat or racket is the best place for it to strike the ball.

entries.clue: Decorative case retained in perpetuity (4)

indicatorNotes.retained in: the answer is kept inside the next word

blocks.note: the four letters sit in the middle of the word, straight after PERP

annotation.surface: A fancy box kept for ever.
annotation.walkthrough: An etui is a small ornamental case for needles or cosmetics, a word met far more in crosswords than elsewhere.
annotation.definitionFit: An etui is a small ornamental case for holding needles, scissors or toiletries.

entries.clue: Real gut I adapted for binding (8)

indicatorNotes.adapted: the letters are adapted into a new arrangement

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 8 letters

annotation.surface: A surgeon using genuine catgut to sew a wound.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is surgical, and so is the answer: a ligature is a thread tied round a vessel, once made of real gut.
annotation.definitionFit: A ligature is something used for binding or tying.

entries.clue: Calm day before noon (4)

indicatorNotes.before: before means coming earlier, so EVE is placed ahead of N

blocks.note: the eve is the day before, as in Christmas Eve
N = noon

annotation.surface: A peaceful morning.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Day before noon' reads as the morning, but 'day before' is EVE and noon is just N.
annotation.definitionFit: Even means calm and steady, as in an even temper.

entries.clue: Like living beings, so alarming somehow (10)

indicatorNotes.somehow: the letters are rearranged in some unstated way

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 10 letters

annotation.surface: Something eerily lifelike, and frightening for it.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface hints at a creepy, lifelike robot, and the definition fits that too.
annotation.definitionFit: Organismal means relating to organisms, living beings.

entries.clue: Track by a wedding venue singer (6)

indicatorNotes.by: RY stands by, next to, CANA

blocks.note: Cana, where Jesus turned water into wine at a wedding
RY = railway, a track

annotation.surface: A song track played beside a wedding venue, singer in tow.
annotation.walkthrough: The wedding at Cana is from the Gospel of John; the answer's 'singer' is the bird, not a vocalist.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: the canary is kept for its song, and in underworld slang a canary is also an informer who 'sings'.

entries.clue: Drink in university knocked back without a song (3,5)

indicatorNotes.knocked back: MIT is knocked back, reading TIM

blocks.note: the Massachusetts Institute of Technology
used as it stands
an aria is a song in an opera

annotation.surface: A drink downed at college, then a song.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Knocked back' is drinking talk, and here it reverses MIT; 'without' means outside, so the reversed TIM goes round A.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: Tia Maria is a brand of Jamaican coffee liqueur.

entries.clue: This setter wears very poor coats (6)

indicatorNotes.wears: I wears PANTS, sitting inside them

blocks.note: pants is British slang for rubbish, very poor
the setter speaking of himself

annotation.surface: The setter owns shabby overcoats.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Coats' reads as clothing next to 'wears', but it is the verb: paints coats a wall. 'Pants' in British slang means rubbish.
annotation.definitionFit: To paint something is to coat it.

entries.clue: Where to buy cheaper booze on board (5)

indicatorNotes.on board: ALE goes aboard SS, a steamship, sitting inside it

blocks.note: SS = steamship
ale is beer, booze

annotation.surface: Duty-free drink on a ferry.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface points at duty-free, but the answer is the sales, when shops cut their prices; 'on board' is the convention for putting something inside SS.
annotation.definitionFit: The sales are where goods can be bought at reduced prices.

entries.clue: Gets up and down (4)

indicatorNotes.up and down: in a down entry the answer reads the same upwards and downwards

blocks.note: a down answer that reads the same whether taken upwards or downwards

annotation.surface: Someone rising and descending, as on a seesaw.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Gets up' looks like a phrase for rising, but 'Gets' alone is the definition and 'up and down' says the down entry reads the same both ways.
annotation.definitionFit: To get something is to understand it, to see it.

entries.clue: Poe’s subject and novel are brutal, impure (9,6)

indicatorNotes.novel: the letters are made new, into a fresh order

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 15 letters

annotation.surface: A critic judging Poe's themes and his novel harsh and unclean.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Novel' pretends to be a book by Poe, who wrote short stories; it is the anagram indicator. 'The Premature Burial' is his 1844 tale of being buried alive.
annotation.definitionFit: Premature burial, being buried alive, is the subject of Poe's story of that name.

entries.clue: Flower borders thought extremely shabby (5)

indicatorNotes.borders: TAY borders TT, lying on both sides
indicatorNotes.extremely: only the extremes, first and last letters, of thought are used

blocks.note: a flower is something that flows, a river; the Tay is in Scotland
the outer letters of ThoughT

annotation.surface: A garden's flower borders thought to be very scruffy.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Flower borders' reads as garden beds; the flower is a river, the Tay, and it borders the TT.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: something worn out and scruffy is tatty in informal British English.

entries.clue: Crude experiences entertaining the French (9)

indicatorNotes.entertaining: TASTES entertains LES, holding it inside

blocks.note: to taste something is to experience it
les is French for 'the' (plural)

annotation.surface: Vulgar adventures laid on to amuse French visitors.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Entertaining' looks like 'amusing' but means holding inside.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the sense of vulgar: a crude remark is one in poor taste.
